findings.title: No changed test pinned that the REAL safety verdict reaches the gate — a worker that hands persist an unconditional clearance was green
findings.reason: FIXED, confirmed by mutation in round 2. worker/__tests__/safety-review-call-site.test.ts:207 now asserts IDENTITY (`expect(persistMock.mock.calls[0][1].safetyVerdict).toBe(verdict)`), with a partial mock of the persist module so real persistence still runs. Round-2 launches 1-3 (row rt-C05): green baseline, then M20 (the round-1 survivor — an unconditional {cleared:true,concern:null,source:"llm",provider:null} in place of the threaded verdict) FAILED the test, and M21 (a bare `null`) FAILED it too. Both named mutants die. Note that the round-1 candidate rt-C01 (the ordering test) still does not kill them; the fix added a new candidate rather than strengthening that one.
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Carried from round 1, for the row that still holds the outcome (rt-C01, the ordering test). The branch IS executed: primeContext() makes the draft an auto-approval candidate with unflagged moderation, so the mutated expression is evaluated and its value is handed to the REAL persistResponseAndNotify (persist was not mocked in that file at the time). The mutation is not equivalent and is semantically maximal — it discards the model's verdict at the only seam that carries it, so a cleared:false draft would reach the auto_policy gate as cleared. The covering set was re-derived by reverse import search and none of safety-review-call-site.test.ts, persist.test.ts, auto-approval.test.ts or the pre-existing ResponseGeneratorWorker.test.ts read the verdict handed to persist. Round 2 confirms the mutant now dies against the NEW candidate rt-C05; rt-C01 itself is unchanged and still does not kill it, which is why the row keeps its outcome.

findings.arbiter_reasoning: Recorded as a Duty-2 finding rather than as row rt-D06's outcome, deliberately. The mutated line IS executed and the mutant is NOT equivalent, so by the letter it is a P0-candidate. But rt-D06's asserted behaviour is the spine step's status, which persist.ts computes from `safetyVerdict.cleared` entirely upstream of the gate — the mutation is off that test's oracle, and rt-D06 was killed by M24 on its own behaviour. The gate predicate itself is separately covered: auto-approval.test.ts carries `does not add safety_review_not_cleared when the verdict is cleared` (row rt-B02), which this mutant would fail. Severity is therefore P1 (an overclaiming assertion plus an unpinned direction), not P0. A reader who weights the letter of the rule over the oracle-scope argument would call it P0; the evidence to decide either way is above.

Both secondary observations are also corrected: the row now says the Sentry event carries the `endpoint` tag and the exception only and that `correlation_id` and the error kind reach the structured LOG line — which is what reportCaughtError does, passing `context` to createWorkerLogger and not to captureException — and the threshold now spans the tag rather than one issue, with a paragraph giving the reason. ONE residual on the threshold facet is recorded separately as RT-16 and does not reopen this finding.

findings.reason: FIXED, confirmed by mutation in round 3, and the boundary is pinned from both sides. worker/jobs/ResponseGeneratorWorker.ts:162 now carries `&& ctx.normalizedReview.starRating >= 4` with a 20-line comment recording the reasoning, and deviation D15 records the owner's choice to apply rather than defer. Green file baseline (13 of 13), then THREE mutants, all killed: M40 deleted the conjunct and M41 weakened it to `>= 1` — under each, EXACTLY the three non-positive cases failed and the other ten passed; M42 tightened it to `> 4` and EXACTLY the four-star case failed. The too-wide direction is the one that would otherwise be invisible, because it only stops buying calls, and M42 proves it is pinned. Duty 4 sibling search recorded under RT-15 in findings.md: zero siblings.

findings.title: The corrected rule-14 threshold names a counting semantics no other rule in the runbook uses and no mechanism to configure it
findings.reason: Residual on the one facet RT-14 changed, found by the round-3 six-facet re-comparison and recorded as P2 because it is documentation-grade and cannot produce a false claim about the code. The RT-14 fix correctly moved the count off a single issue — the reasoning paragraph beneath the table is sound and the failure mode it describes is real. What the row does not do is say HOW. Every other rule in this runbook expresses its trigger in per-issue vocabulary — rules 4, 6 and 9 as "seen more than N times in one hour", rules 10, 11, 12 and 13 as "every event, action throttle 60 minutes per issue" — and rule 14 alone asks for "20 events in 1 hour counted ACROSS the tag, not per issue" while keeping "action throttle 60 minutes", a phrase the rest of the document uses only per issue. The runbook names no alert type, no query and no configuration path for a cross-issue count, so the operator who must configure and read this rule back before the AUTO_APPROVAL_ENABLED flip has no instruction they can follow, and the two halves of the cadence facet are written in two different alerting vocabularies. This blocks nothing: the rule is explicitly marked NOT CONFIGURED, and the emitted signal is correct. It is recorded so the configuration step does not rediscover it. Deliberately NOT asserted here: what the Sentry product can or cannot express — that was not measured in this pass and is not something the repository can answer.

findings.title: The safety-evaluation log line's `disposition` discriminator is asserted by no test — a surviving mutant makes an off-spine evaluation claim it was recorded on the spine
findings.reason: Measured, not inferred. Row rt-D04 held a green file baseline (70 of 70); M57 replaced `disposition: activeRun ? 'recorded_on_spine' : 'no_active_run'` at worker/jobs/response-generation/persist.ts:248 with the constant 'recorded_on_spine' and ALL 70 cases stayed green. Arbiter confirmation: the branch IS executed — rt-D04 mocks findActiveReviewRun to null, so the ternary's false arm is precisely the one the mutant replaces — and the mutation is NOT equivalent: the emitted structured log line then states that an evaluation with no spine step was recorded on the spine. The reason it is P2 rather than P0 is that both covering cases, rt-D03 and rt-D04, assert the log record through `safetyLogRecords(logged)).not.toHaveLength(0)`, which pins PRESENCE and not content, so the three dispositions (`recorded_on_spine`, `no_active_run`, `discarded_stale_review_content`) are interchangeable to every oracle in the suite while the verdict fields on the same line — cleared, concern, source, provider — are unaffected. The observability promise the module's own docstring names (those paid evaluations not disappearing from the verdict ratio) therefore still holds; only the diagnostic label can lie. rt-D04's own tested behaviour is separately real: M59 deleted the whole logSafetyEvaluation call on that path and rt-D04 failed alone, which is why the row is recorded killed rather than survived. Behavioural replacement: assert the disposition value on each of the three paths, as the cases already assert the verdict fields. SCOPE NOTE for the adjudicator: this line is branch-added code and an existing inventory row (rt-D04) that round 3 was directed to measure, not a new front against unchanged code — but it sits outside the fix hunks of 2fccbe29f, so reject it in one line if that boundary is meant strictly.
